title: Cabinet approves Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme for Development of Intra-State Transmission System with Battery Energy Storage Systems
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 SEP 2026 3:12PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III
(GEC-III) scheme. This historic initiative will strengthen India’s Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) to enable evacuation of up to 135 Gigawatt (GW) of renewable energy across States/ Union Territories.
The scheme also provides for deployment of 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) at the Renewable Energy (RE) developer/generator end or any other location of importance for grid flexibility to address intermittency, congestion, peak-hour curtailment and meet non-solar hour demand. The scheme will facilitate grid integration and power evacuation with in the States/UTs of India.
The scheme is targeted to be set up by FY 2032-33 with total project outlay of Rs.1,86,405 crore, comprising Rs.1,36,378 crore for the development of Intra-State Transmission Systems (InSTS) under GEC-III, Rs.50,000 crore for 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The Scheme involves a total Central Financial Support of Rs.54,082 crore. The Central Financial Assistance (CFA) will help in offsetting the Intra-State transmission charges and thus keep the power costs down. Thus, the Government support will ultimately benefit the end users – the citizens of India.
All Greenfield projects under the InSTS component will be implemented through Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mode, while brownfield upgradation and network strengthening works will be executed under Cost Plus Basis (CPB). The State Transmission Utilities will be the overall implementing agency, and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) will participate under TBCB on a Build-Own-Operate-Maintain (BOOM) model.
The scheme will help in achieving the target of 900 GW installed Non-Fossil capacity by 2035. The scheme will also contribute to long term energy security of the country and promote ecologically sustainable growth by reducing carbon footprint. It will generate large direct & indirect employment in the power sector, manufacturing, and construction industries. Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing and deployment will additionally generate employment in the domestic energy storage industry. The scheme will also generate long-term skilled employment in operation, maintenance, and grid management across participating States.

title: Cabinet approves One Network, Smarter Traffic: Delhi Moves to Real-Time Traffic Management
subtitle:
Rs.1,789.52 crore approved for Intelligent Traffic Management System for Delhi

AI-enabled adaptive traffic signals, technology-based enforcement and real-time traffic information to make travel safer, smoother and more efficient 42 traffic corridors of Delhi to be covered in three phases

System to facilitate priority movement of ambulances and quicker response to congestion and road incidents
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 SEP 2026 3:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the  Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved implementation of the ITMS Project by Delhi Police at an estimated cost of Rs.1,789.52 crore, inclusive of taxes. The project will cover 42 identified traffic corridors and will be implemented in three phases over 24 months, followed by five years of operation and maintenance.
As part of the wider efforts of the Central Government and the Government of NCT of Delhi to improve traffic management, transport infrastructure and urban mobility in the National Capital, a major technology-led initiative will now be taken up through the Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS). The project will enable Delhi’s existing road network to be managed more intelligently through real-time traffic data, adaptive traffic signals, automated enforcement and integrated command-and-control systems.
Delhi has around 71 lakh active registered vehicles. Vehicular growth has substantially outpaced expansion of road infrastructure, while traffic regulation continues to depend significantly on fixed signal timings and manual intervention. The ITMS seeks to make better use of the available road capacity by enabling traffic management to respond dynamically to actual conditions on the road.
Benefits:
Smarter traffic signals and smoother movement:
Adaptive Traffic Control Systems will dynamically adjust signal timings according to prevailing traffic conditions and coordinate signals along identified corridors, helping reduce avoidable stoppages and delays.
Priority for ambulances and emergency vehicles:
The system will facilitate green corridors and priority movement for emergency vehicles, enabling faster passage through congested stretches.
Faster response to congestion and accidents:
Real-time detection of congestion, slow-moving traffic and road incidents will enable quicker diversions and operational response by Delhi Police.
Timely information for commuters:
Variable Message Sign boards and digital platforms will provide information on congestion, diversions, parking availability and traffic conditions. Information may also be shared with navigation service providers, helping commuters make better travel choices.
More consistent and technology-based enforcement:
The system will strengthen automated detection of violations such as red-light and stop-line violations, speeding, wrong-way driving, non-use of helmets and seat belts, illegal parking and use of mobile phones while driving. AI-based analytics will also assist in identifying stolen, hot-listed and blacklisted vehicles, repeat violators and vehicles connected with hit-and-run incidents.
Integrated city-wide traffic management:
Traffic regulation, enforcement and information dissemination will be brought together on a common platform through Traffic Command and Control Centres, supported by secure Data Centre and Disaster Recovery infrastructure. The system will follow open standards and APIs to enable future integration and scalability.
The project will cover 1,092 Adaptive Traffic Control System and 1,029 enforcement locations. Implementation will be performance-driven, with each subsequent phase to be taken up after evaluation of the preceding phase against prescribed testing, commissioning, acceptance and performance parameters.
Delhi Police will implement the project through a Master System Integrator selected through competitive bidding. C-DAC will provide technical support as Project Management Consultant, including technical scrutiny, monitoring, validation and acceptance during implementation and operation and maintenance.
The ITMS will complement ongoing efforts to improve Delhi’s road and transport infrastructure by providing the technology and real-time intelligence required to use the existing road network more efficiently. The project is expected to contribute to smoother traffic movement, safer roads, quicker incident response, more effective enforcement and a more predictable travel experience for citizens.

title: Ayush Emerges as One of India’s Fastest-Growing Service Sectors, RIS Study Estimates US$36.92 Billion Economy
subtitle:
Ayush services sector records 16.91% CAGR since FY23; supports 1.76 million livelihoods and generates US$1.77 billion in Medical Value Travel revenue

Ayush services sector projected to scale to US$216–318 billion by 2047, emerging as a major contributor to Viksit Bharat
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 SEP 2026 12:38PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ayush services sector has emerged as one of India’s fastest-growing service sectors, with its economic contribution estimated at US$36.92 billion in FY2024-25, according to a new study by the Research and Information System for Developing Countries (RIS). Registering a 16.91 per cent CAGR since FY2022-23, the sector is increasingly contributing to India’s economic growth through healthcare, wellness, employment generation and Medical Value Travel. The study projects that the Ayush services economy could scale to US$216–318 billion by 2047, underlining its significant potential to contribute to the Viksit Bharat @2047 vision. The Report was formally released during the 11th Ayurveda Day celebrations in Nagpur on 23rd September.
Shri Prataprao Jadhav, Union Minister of State (IC) for Ayush and Minister of State for Health & Family Welfare, emphasised that the findings mark a significant milestone in recognising the Ayush sector's economic potential. The Minister stated, “The findings of this landmark study affirm that Ayush is not merely a cultural inheritance but a dynamic and high-growth engine of India’s economy. The Ayush sector is poised to play an increasingly important role in healthcare, wellness, employment and global economic engagement, while contributing to our vision of a healthy and self-reliant India.”
Secretary, Ministry of Ayush Vaidya Rajesh Kotecha stated, “For the first time, the economic contribution of the Ayush services sector has been measured through a nationally scaled, establishment-level survey covering all major Ayush systems. The report provides a robust evidence base to guide future investment, policy planning and reforms.”
Professor Sachin Kumar Sharma, Director General, RIS, highlighted, “This study marks an important step in building an evidence-based understanding of India’s Ayush services economy. Based on a nationally scaled survey of 15,914 establishments across all six Ayush systems, the findings show that an economy of US$36.92 billion, growing at close to 17 per cent annually and supporting 1.76 million livelihoods, is no longer a peripheral sector but a dynamic, knowledge-based service economy.”
According to the study, the Ayush services economy was estimated at US$36.92 billion in FY25, registering a Compound Annual Growth Rate (CAGR) of 16.91 per cent since FY23. The findings underline the emergence of Ayush services as a significant and rapidly growing segment of India’s services economy, with substantial potential for further expansion through organised healthcare delivery, wellness services, quality infrastructure and global outreach.
The study shows that clinics and day-care centres constitute the core of the Ayush services economy, together accounting for more than 71 per cent of total sectoral revenue. Standalone clinics generated an estimated US$16.21 billion, while day-care centres contributed US$10.13 billion. Ayurveda remained the largest individual system, accounting for US$17.73 billion, or nearly 48 per cent of the sector’s total revenue.
The report also highlights the growing economic significance of the Ayush-based wellness segment, including yoga centres, spas and resorts offering Ayush-based services. The segment recorded a 21.29 per cent CAGR, with yoga centres registering around 75 per cent growth in revenue over two years, reflecting rising demand for preventive health, wellness and holistic care services.
The study finds that Ayush services sector has emerged as a significant source of employment. Sector directly supports 1.76 million livelihoods, with more than one million jobs concentrated in local and standalone clinics. Women account for 43 per cent of the overall Ayush services workforce, with female participation exceeding 50 per cent in several organised segments. Women constitute over 60 per cent of the workforce in wellness settings (spas and resorts) offering Ayush-based services, 58 per cent in educational institutions, 57 per cent in day-care centres and 53 per cent in hospitals.
The study further points to the growing potential of Ayush in Medical Value Travel (MVT). The sector generated an estimated US$1.77 billion in MVT revenue in FY25. While international patients account for only around 5 per cent of patient volumes, they contribute an estimated 15–25 per cent of hospital-segment revenues. The study notes that Ayush therapeutic programmes, including Panchakarma and residential Yoga, are associated with longer patient stays, with an average length of stay ranging from 5 to 11 days.
Digital visibility and quality accreditation are also emerging as important factors in attracting international patients. According to the study, establishments with a dedicated functional website have 3.6 times higher odds of attracting international patients, while recognised quality accreditation such as NABH or ISO is associated with a doubling of such odds.
Looking ahead, the study projects significant growth potential for the sector as India advances towards Viksit Bharat @2047. The Ayush services economy could expand from the estimated US$36.92 billion in FY25 to US$216 billion–US$318 billion by 2047, subject to the strengthening of infrastructure, quality systems, skills, digital capabilities and international market access.
The study outlines a strategic pathway backed by an analysis through four pillars: — knowledge  value chain of Ayush; enterprise and institutional capabilities;  global competitiveness and Medical Value Travel;  innovation through digital technologies and Artificial Intelligence. It also emphasises the need for wider quality accreditation, digital health records, workforce skilling, international readiness and responsible adoption of emerging technologies.
The findings reinforce the expanding role of Ayush not only as a healthcare and wellness ecosystem but also as a contributor to employment generation, entrepreneurship, services-led economic growth and India’s growing global engagement in traditional and complementary medicine.
The RIS study provides an evidence-based assessment of the evolving Ayush services landscape and identifies opportunities for strengthening the sector’s contribution to India’s healthcare, wellness and economic development priorities in the years ahead.

The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has released findings of Independent Drive Test (IDT) conducted across Sonitpur district in the state of Assam under Assam LSA, during the month of August 2026, for information of general telecom consumers. The purpose of this drive test is to assess and verify real time quality of mobile network services (both voice & data) provided by Telecom Service Providers (TSPs). During the IDT, TRAI captures performance of TSPs for key Quality of Service (QoS) parameters like Coverage, Call Drop Rate (CDR), Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), data Download (DL) and Upload (UL) throughput etc., which are then published to inform Consumers and encourage TSPs to improve their services.
These IDTs have been designed to capture on ground mobile network performance of all TSPs across diverse usages environment like cities, hotspots, public transport hubs, etc. In this type of drive testing, live data and voice sessions are established using SIM cards from all TSPs over 2G, 3G, 4G, and 5G networks. Multiple advanced test handsets are used, and the sessions are monitored and analysed in real-time using advanced Software Systems.
TRAI, through its appointed agency, conducted drive tests across City drive – 308.0 KMs, Hotspot locations - 10, Walk Test – 1.6 KMs in Assam LSA during 10th August 2026 to 13th August 2026 in Assam LSA. These tests were conducted under the supervision of the TRAI Regional Office Kolkata. b)    Voice Services: Call Setup Success Rate (CSSR), Drop Call Rate (DCR), Call Setup Time, Call Silence Rate, Speech Quality (MOS).

title: OPERATION DRISHTI: Armed Forces Medical Services Conduct Two Landmark Mega Eye Surgical Camps in Kashmir
subtitle: 364 Sight-Restoring Eye Surgeries Performed Across Tangdhar and Srinagar
date:

                30 SEP 2026 8:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 11th Mega Eye Surgical Camp under Operation Drishti concluded at 92 Base Hospital, Srinagar, on September 30, 2026, bringing the Kashmir leg of the initiative to a successful close. Across the two mega eye camps conducted at Tangdhar and Srinagar, the surgical team from Army Hospital (Research & Referral) (AHRR), under the leadership of Brigadier Sanjay Kumar Mishra, performed 364 eye surgeries, including cataract, glaucoma, pterygium and retinal procedures.
In the weeks preceding the surgical camps, teams from 92 Base Hospital and 328 Field Hospital conducted 18 screening camps across remote and forward areas of the Kashmir Valley, including Tangdhar, Dawar, Machil, Uri, Baramulla, Bandipora, Khanabal and Kangan. Nearly 6,000 people were screened, with around 500 patients identified as requiring surgical intervention. The beneficiaries were subsequently treated in two phases under Operation Drishti.
The first phase was conducted at Tangdhar, in the sensitive sector along the Line of Control (LoC). The camp, held from September 24-25, 2026, marked the first-ever mega eye surgical camp conducted at the LoC in an underground operation theatre. The surgical team successfully performed 220 sight-restoring surgeries over two days, demonstrating the capability to provide advanced ophthalmic care even in remote and operationally challenging locations.
The second phase was conducted at 92 Base Hospital, Srinagar, from September 28-29, 2026, where 144 patients underwent eye surgeries. Several patients with severely impaired vision experienced significant improvement, with some regaining clear vision as early as the following day. In addition to cataract surgeries, the camp provided specialised procedures including glued IOL implantation, glaucoma surgery, pterygium excision and retinal interventions for diabetic retinopathy.

title: NBA to Mark 23rd Foundation Day tomorrow with significant progress in Access and Benefit Sharing
subtitle: Over Rs. 278 Crore realised through ABS; More than Rs. 200 Crore disbursed for Biodiversity Conservation and Community Benefits
ministry: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 SEP 2026 9:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) will mark its 23rd Foundation Day tomorrow, 01.10.2026, with significant progress in translating Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) into tangible outcomes for biodiversity conservation and local communities. Since 2008, the NBA has realised over Rs. 278 crore through ABS and disbursed more than Rs. 200 crore towards biodiversity conservation and the benefit of communities, farmers, institutions and other benefit claimants across the country. This progress reflects the strengthening of India’s ABS framework and its ability to connect the use of biological resources with conservation and equitable sharing of benefits. India has emerged as a pioneer in operationalising ABS, supported by a three-tier institutional architecture comprising the NBA at the national level, State Biodiversity Boards (SBBs) and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils (UTBCs) at the State and Union Territory levels, and Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs) at the local level, in accordance with the Biological Diversity Act, 2002.
As the NBA marks its 23rd Foundation Day tomorrow, this progress reflects the evolution of ABS into an important instrument for translating the value of biological diversity into conservation action and community benefits. The impact is reflected in a wide network of beneficiaries. The more than Rs. 200 crore disbursed by the NBA has supported over 10,500 BMCs, 28 SBBs, 7 UTBCs, 6 Forest Departments and 58 research institutions and universities across the country for biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, research, capacity building and community-oriented activities. Between 01.09.2025 and 31.08.2026, the NBA received Rs. 12.93 crore in ABS amounts and released Rs. 132.01 crore to States, Union Territories, institutions, farmers, local communities and other identified benefit claimants. The releases included accumulated ABS amounts from earlier collections, enabling support for a wider range of conservation and livelihood initiatives.
The ABS mechanism covers a diverse range of biological resources, including agricultural and horticultural crops, plant genetic resources, medicinal and aromatic plants, livestock genetic resources, Red Sanders and microorganisms. Contributions have been received from sectors including seeds, AYUSH, pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals, biotechnology, cosmetics, chemicals, biofuels, and food and beverages. Companies such as Nunhems India, East West Seeds India, Pioneer Overseas Corporation, Bayer Bioscience, Himalaya Wellness Company, Dabur India, Organic India, Laurus Labs, Akay Natural Ingredients, Novozymes South Asia, Advanced Enzymes and L’Oréal India, among others, have contributed to the ABS mechanism in accordance with the applicable legal framework.
The benefits are increasingly reaching the ground, supporting the conservation and sustainable use of maize, rice, turmeric, amla, mustard, bitter gourd, cotton, okra and chilli, as well as medicinal and aromatic resources such as kalmegh, elachi, tulsi, guggal gum, neem, garcinia, ashwagandha, pepper and lavanga. Recent releases include Rs. 6.67 crore for 25,431 cotton varieties, Rs. 15.52 crore for mustard-related conservation and Rs. 3.51 crore for 139 okra varieties and 28 hybrids. Around Rs. 100 crore has also been released for the conservation and protection of Red Sanders through the Andhra Pradesh Forest Department and Andhra Pradesh State Biodiversity Board, demonstrating how ABS can translate the value of biological resources into tangible conservation outcomes. At the State and Union Territory levels, over Rs. 51 crore has been generated through ABS approvals granted by SBBs and UTBCs to Section 7 entities (Indian entities) for commercial utilisation of biological resources.
ABS funds are also supporting People’s Biodiversity Registers, habitat restoration, conservation of traditional varieties, medicinal plant conservation, community gene banks, capacity building and sustainable livelihood activities. Where individual benefit claimants cannot be identified, the framework provides for utilisation of funds for the socio-economic development of areas from which biological resources originate. Regulatory reforms and digitalisation have strengthened ease of doing business and ease of compliance, while safeguarding the objectives of biodiversity conservation and fair and equitable benefit sharing. The ABS e-filing system has simplified application processing and improved transparency and tracking. As of now, the NBA has received 11,273 applications, with 6,074 agreements signed/approvals granted and 2,098 certificates issued. Model agreements, standardised procedures and online services have further made the ABS process more predictable and user-friendly. ABS obligations are incorporated into agreements executed by the NBA, providing a clear basis for benefit-sharing payments under the applicable ABS Regulations.
By linking biodiversity conservation with sustainable livelihoods, ABS is contributing to local value addition, sustainable use of biological resources, community participation and livelihood opportunities, particularly in biodiversity-rich rural and tribal areas. It also contributes to the vision of Viksit Bharat @2047 and complements initiatives such as PM-JANMAN, the Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission and Van Dhan, which promote tribal welfare and natural-resource-based livelihoods. India’s ABS framework gives practical effect to the principles of the Nagoya Protocol and advances the country’s commitments under the NBSAP 2024–2030 and the KMGBF, particularly Target 13 on fair and equitable benefit sharing. Through conservation, sustainable use and community benefits, ABS also supports KMGBF Targets 4, 5 and 9 and contributes to relevant SDGs, strengthening the link between biodiversity, livelihoods and sustainable development.
With the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, as amended in 2023, the Biological Diversity Rules, 2024 and the Biological Diversity (Access and Benefit Sharing) Regulations, 2025, India continues to strengthen a transparent, predictable and effective ABS system, facilitating legitimate access and compliance while ensuring that benefits arising from the utilisation of biological resources contribute to conservation and community well-being. As the NBA marks its 23rd Foundation Day tomorrow, 01.10.2026, it will continue to work with SBBs, UTBCs, BMCs, line departments, research institutions, industry, local communities and other stakeholders to further strengthen ABS implementation. India’s experience demonstrates that ABS can serve as a practical bridge among biodiversity conservation, sustainable use, innovation and community well-being, ensuring that the value generated from India’s biological wealth contributes to its conservation and to the people who sustain it.

title: Delhi Records Lowest September Average AQI in Five Years; Air Quality Improvement Trend Continues in 2026

content:
The improving trend in the overall air quality of Delhi-NCR continues, with Delhi recording its lowest monthly average Air Quality Index (AQI) for September during the current year, as compared to the corresponding period of the last five years, from 2022 to 2026.
The monthly average AQI of Delhi for September during the current year has been recorded at 102, as against 105 in 2025, 105 in 2024, 108 in 2023 and 104 in 2022.
The period from January to September 2026 witnessed the highest number of days with daily average AQI less than 200 (‘Moderate’ category) during the last five years. Delhi recorded 194 such days in 2026, as against 187 days in 2025, 188 days in 2024, 193 days in 2023 and 146 days in 2022.
The period from January to September 2026 also witnessed the lowest number of ‘Poor to Severe+’ days during the last five years, with 79 days in 2026, as against 86 days in 2025, 86 days in 2024, 80 days in 2023 and 127 days in 2022.
The period from January to September 2026 (up to 28.09.2026) has witnessed the joint-lowest average PM2.5 concentration in Delhi compared to the corresponding period since 2022. Delhi recorded an average PM2.5 concentration of 69 µg/m³ in 2026, as against 69 µg/m³ in 2025, 81 µg/m³ in 2024, 73 µg/m³ in 2023 and 80 µg/m³ in 2022.
The Commission for Air Quality Management (CAQM) is working closely with various stakeholders concerned to take effective measures for the prevention, control and abatement of air pollution and to improve air quality in Delhi-NCR. The Sub-committee took stock of the preparedness of Punjab, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh for implementation of Direction No. 99 dated 15.05.2026 and the respective action plans for prevention and control of paddy stubble burning during 2026, with the objective of complete elimination of such incidents. The review also covered measures for crop diversification, promotion of Direct Seeded Rice (DSR), utilisation of crop residue and strengthening of awareness and IEC activities among farmers.
The Sub-Committee undertook a comprehensive review of measures for abatement of vehicular pollution, including actions envisaged under Direction No. 88 dated 23.04.2025, as amended on 17.10.2025, relating to restrictions on entry of BS-IV and below transport and commercial goods vehicles into Delhi. The implementation of Direction No. 93 dated 03.06.2025 concerning migration of buses entering Delhi, including buses operating under All India Tourist Permit and other service regimes, towards cleaner modes was also reviewed.
The meeting further examined the preparedness of NCR State Governments/ GNCTD for installation of Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) systems at Fuel/ CNG stations, in accordance with Direction No. 101 dated 15.05.2026, for enforcement of restrictions on fuelling of vehicles without valid Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) in NCR with effect from 01.10.2026. The Sub-Committee also reviewed enforcement of Direction No. 94 dated 03.06.2025, as amended on 23.12.2025, for fast-tracking cleaner mobility in services provided by motor vehicle aggregators, delivery service providers and e-Commerce entities, including compliance verification through surprise checks.
The status of enforcement against older End-of-Life (EoL) vehicles, in compliance with the Supreme Court of India’s order dated 17.12.2025 was also deliberated upon, with emphasis on intensifying action for impounding and scrapping of such vehicles. Further, the sub-committee reviewed progress towards complete phasing out of diesel auto-rickshaws from NCR Districts by 31.12.2026 in accordance with Direction No. 70 dated 30.11.2022. Measures for identification and decongestion of traffic congestion hotspots/ intersections in Delhi and NCR towns were also reviewed, including deployment of Integrated Traffic Management Systems (ITMS) with ANPR-based automated challaning.
The Sub-Committee also reviewed the status of implementation of Direction No. 103 dated 19.08.2026 regarding prevention and control of air pollution from stone crushing units in NCR. Implementation of Direction No. 98 dated 20.02.2026 relating to stringent emission standards for industries across Delhi-NCR was also reviewed.
With winter season approaching, the meeting accorded focused attention on procurement of additional Mechanical Road Sweeping Machines (MRSMs) and their deployment before commencement of the winter season, particularly for removal of dust from identified dust hotspots.
The Sub-Committee further took stock of the Action Taken Report on incognito/surprise inspections of C&D sites, industries and DG sets, as part of strengthened compliance monitoring and enforcement of the commission’s statutory directions. The meeting also reviewed the status of timely resolution of complaints received through social media platforms and tagged by CPCB to the concerned agencies in GNCTD and NCR States, in accordance with the Directions of the Supreme Court of India.
The concerned implementing agencies were emphasized upon to ensure strict, coordinated and time-bound implementation of the commission’s statutory directions, with particular focus on preparedness for the forthcoming winter season, effective enforcement in the vehicular and industrial sectors, prevention of stubble burning, mitigation of road and C&D dust and strengthening of inspection and compliance-monitoring mechanisms across NCR.
The Sub-Committee reiterated the importance of sustained and coordinated efforts by all concerned agencies to ensure effective implementation of sector-specific measures and to strengthen enforcement mechanisms. Further, all implementing agencies reaffirmed their commitment to undertake strict, targeted and time-bound actions for effective implementation of the Commission’s Directions.

title: Union Minister for Health and Family Welfare Shri J.P. Nadda Addresses World Congress of Gastroenterology 2026 in New Delhi
subtitle:
India Advancing Towards Holistic and Inclusive Healthcare with Greater Emphasis on Prevention and Health Promotion: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda



More Than 600 million Beneficiaries Covered Under AB-PMJAY, Providing ₹5 Lakh Health Cover Per Family: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda



India Recorded 86% Decline in Maternal Mortality Between 1990 and 2023: Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda



Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda Highlights Government’s Comprehensive Approach to Healthcare at WCOG 2026
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 SEP 2026 9:07PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister for Health & Family Welfare, Shri J.P. Nadda, today addressed the World Congress of Gastroenterology (WCOG 2026) in New Delhi. Being held in India for the first time, the four-day international Congress commenced today and will continue till 3 October 2026, bringing together leading experts, clinicians, researchers and healthcare professionals from India and across the world.
With the theme “
Transforming Gastrointestinal Health, Preserving Nature
,” WCOG 2026 is jointly hosted by the Indian Society of Gastroenterology (ISG) and the World Gastroenterology Organisation (WGO), in collaboration with the Indian National Association for Study of the Liver (INASL), Crohn’s and Colitis Foundation India (CCFI), Indian Pancreas Club (IPC) and Indian Neurogastroenterology and Motility Association (INMA). The Congress focuses on advances in gastrointestinal health through cutting-edge science, clinical practice, research, innovation and multidisciplinary exchange.
Addressing the inaugural session, Union Health Minister Shri J.P. Nadda highlighted the Government’s efforts towards bringing about a comprehensive and holistic approach to healthcare, with greater emphasis on preventive and promotive healthcare alongside curative, rehabilitative and palliative care.
Shri Nadda said that, ‘Under leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the National Health Policy of 2017 marked an important shift towards a comprehensive, holistic and inclusive approach to healthcare, encompassing preventive, promotive, curative and rehabilitative dimensions. Under the policy framework, the Government is strengthening health systems across all levels of care, with emphasis on achieving an optimal balance between primary, secondary and tertiary healthcare and strengthening linkages between different levels of care.
Furthermore, He also highlighted the role of Ayushman Arogya Mandirs in strengthening primary healthcare and promoting preventive and promotive health services. He said that the network of around 1.86 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs is serving as an important point of contact for people and is helping bring comprehensive primary healthcare closer to communities.
Shri Nadda underlined that screening for non-communicable diseases (NCDs) is an important pillar of preventive healthcare. Through Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, population-based screening is being undertaken for people aged 30 years and above for hypertension, diabetes and common cancers, including oral, breast and cervical cancers.
He informed that more than 420 million screenings for hypertension, 420 million for diabetes, 360 million for oral cancer, 170 million for breast cancer and 90 million for cervical cancer have been conducted so far.
The Union Health Minister also highlighted the Government’s efforts to promote healthy dietary practices and active lifestyles. He referred to initiatives such as the Eat Right India campaign of FSSAI and Poshan Maah, which seek to create greater awareness about healthy eating habits and physical activity. He also recalled the Prime Minister’s call to citizens to reduce oil consumption as part of efforts to address obesity and promote healthier lifestyles.
Highlighting the progress made in maternal and child health, Shri Nadda noted that institutional deliveries have increased from 79 per cent in 2015-16 to around 90 per cent, as reflected in the National Family Health Survey. He also referred to improvements in maternal and child health outcomes, noting that between 1990 and 2023, India recorded an 86 per cent decline in maternal mortality, while under-five mortality declined by 79 per cent and neonatal mortality by 70 per cent over the respective period.
Shri Nadda further highlighted the Government’s efforts to ensure that financial constraints do not prevent people, particularly those belonging to economically vulnerable and marginalised sections, from accessing quality healthcare. He said that Ayushman Bharat–Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY) was launched in September 2018 with the objective of providing financial protection against hospitalisation and ensuring access to necessary healthcare.
Shri Nadda stated that AB-PMJAY provides health coverage of ₹5 lakh per family per year and has expanded its coverage to more than 600 million beneficiaries, while the scheme has also been extended to around 60 million senior citizens aged 70 years and above, irrespective of their economic status.
He noted that more than 13 crore treatments have been provided under the scheme, involving healthcare expenditure of over ₹2 lakh crore. He said these achievements reflect the scale of the Government’s efforts to make quality healthcare more accessible to citizens.
He also highlighted measures to improve the affordability of medicines and medical devices. Under the Pradhan Mantri Bhartiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana, quality generic medicines are being made available at substantially lower prices compared to branded medicines. He informed that more than 20,149 Jan Aushadhi Kendras are currently serving people across the country and that citizens have collectively saved around ₹45,000 crore on their medicine expenditure through the initiative.
Shri Nadda said that these measures have contributed to reducing the financial burden of healthcare on households. He noted that out-of-pocket expenditure as a proportion of total health expenditure declined from 62 per cent in 2014-15 to 43.4 per cent in 2021-22, reflecting progress towards greater financial protection in healthcare.
He also emphasised that while these achievements provide a strong foundation, continued research and innovation remain essential to address emerging health challenges. He expressed confidence that doctors and researchers working in the field of gastroenterology would contribute innovative solutions to control major gastrointestinal infections and address the evolving burden of gastrointestinal and liver diseases.
Referring to the theme of the Congress, “Transforming Gastrointestinal Health, Preserving Nature,” the Union Health Minister said that the theme is highly relevant in the present context. He expressed confidence that deliberations among leading experts from across the world would contribute to identifying new approaches and solutions for addressing digestive and liver diseases.
Shri Nadda said that international scientific forums such as WCOG provide valuable opportunities for sharing knowledge, learning from different healthcare systems and strengthening international collaboration. He also highlighted the importance of such platforms for young doctors, who would carry forward the next generation of research, clinical practice and innovation in gastroenterology.
Concluding his address, Shri Nadda wished all delegates a successful and productive Congress and invited national and international participants to make full use of the opportunity to exchange knowledge, experiences and ideas during the four-day event.
On the occasion, Shri J.P. Nadda presented Lifetime Achievement Awards to distinguished veterans of the field, recognising their significant contributions to gastroenterology and advancing patient care, research and medical practice.
WCOG 2026 brings together a diverse group of healthcare professionals, including gastroenterologists, hepatologists, pancreatologists, endoscopists, gastrointestinal surgeons, dieticians, nurses, technologists and allied healthcare professionals from across the world. The participation of professionals from different specialties provides an opportunity for exchange of knowledge, experience and best practices.
The Congress also highlights India’s growing contribution to global gastrointestinal research, including in the areas of epidemiology, guidelines and translational medicine. The platform enables Indian and international experts to share research findings, clinical experiences and emerging approaches in gastrointestinal healthcare.
The scientific programme features participation from international and national experts and includes scientific sessions, lectures, debates, workshops, live demonstrations and abstract presentations. The programme also provides opportunities for interaction with industry and technology partners, facilitating discussions on emerging technologies and innovations in gastrointestinal healthcare.
The Congress provides a global platform for knowledge exchange, collaboration and innovation in gastroenterology and allied disciplines. It also offers an opportunity for Indian healthcare professionals, researchers and institutions to engage with the international medical community and contribute to global scientific discussions in the field.
The first-time hosting of the World Congress of Gastroenterology in India marks an important milestone in the country’s engagement with the global gastroenterology community and provides an opportunity to further strengthen international scientific partnerships and multidisciplinary collaboration in healthcare.
Prof. Nikhil Tandon, Director, AIIMS, Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India; Dr. Carolina Olano, President, WGO; Dr. Govind Makharia, Chairman, Local Organising Committee (LOC), WCOG; Dr. Mathew Philip, Secretary General, ISG were also present at the Event.

Union Minister for Heavy Industries and Steel, H. D. Kumaraswamy on Wednesday unveiled and digitally launched the Impact Report of the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) Industry Accelerator Project at Navigyaan 2026 in New Delhi, marking an important milestone in the development and advancement of indigenous technologies for India’s mobility and manufacturing sectors.
Addressing the gathering, H.D. Kumaraswamy said the event marked the conclusion of the MHI Industry Accelerator Project and highlighted the importance of building domestic technological and manufacturing capabilities.
“The Government of India under the visionary leadership of Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modiji, has placed strong emphasis on building domestic technological and manufacturing capabilities,” he said.
The Minister said that the vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat requires India to move beyond being a large market for advanced technologies and develop the capacity to manufacture and export them.
“The vision of Atmanirbhar Bharat calls for an India that is not only a large market for advanced technologies, but also a country that develops, manufactures and exports those,” Kumaraswamy said.
Highlighting the scale of support extended under the Scheme for Enhancement of Competitiveness in the Indian Capital Goods Sector - Phase II, he said the scheme has a total financial outlay of ₹1,207 crore and aims to support common technology development and services infrastructure. Under the scheme, 33 projects have been approved.
The MHI Industry Accelerator Programme, one of these initiatives, provided ₹35.72 crore in Grant-in-Aid for 10 technologies, with the objective of supporting their progression from Technology Readiness Level 3 to Level 9.
Kumaraswamy noted that the technologies supported under the programme cover several areas of future mobility, including electric powertrains, high-voltage motor control and energy storage. An important outcome, he said, has been the movement of technologies from early-stage prototypes towards commercially viable products.
Emphasising the importance of collaboration in technology development, the Minister said government, industry, research institutions, academia, startups and institutions such as ARAI each have an important role in strengthening the innovation ecosystem.
“Government can provide the policy framework and targeted support. Industry brings market understanding and manufacturing capability. Research and academic institutions contribute knowledge and technology. Startups bring new ideas and agility,” he said.
He further underlined the role of institutions such as ARAI in bridging the gap between technology development, validation and industry adoption.
Kumaraswamy said that as India moves towards Viksit Bharat@2047, the focus must remain on developing capabilities within the country and taking Indian technologies to international markets.
“It is this ecosystem that we need to strengthen further. As we move towards Viksit Bharat@2047, our focus should be clear: educate, innovate, manufacture and integrate technologies in India and take Indian technologies to global markets,” he said.
The Minister also stressed that self-reliance should extend beyond import substitution and focus on developing Indian intellectual property, resilient supply chains and skilled human resources.
“The objective of self-reliance is not simply to replace imports. It is to build Indian intellectual property, supply chains and skilled human resources,” Kumaraswamy said.
He called for continued efforts to identify emerging technology requirements, strengthen industry-academia collaboration and develop talent capable of meeting the technological needs of the future.
Concluding his address, Kumaraswamy said India must create an ecosystem that enables innovations to move efficiently through every stage of development.
“Let us continue to build an ecosystem in which Indian innovation can move efficiently from concept to prototype, prototype to product, and product to global market,” he said.
The Minister also felicitated members of the MHI Industry Accelerator Project for their contribution towards taking technologies from development and validation to industrial application and commercialisation. The event, organised as a culmination of the MHI Industry Accelerator Project implemented by ARAI-AMTIF, brought together stakeholders from government, industry, academia, research and the technology ecosystem.
During the programme, Kumaraswamy visited the startup exhibition and reviewed innovations supported under the Accelerator initiative. The technologies showcased at the exhibition covered areas including electric mobility, power electronics, high-voltage systems, energy storage, predictive maintenance, sensors and advanced surface engineering.

title: Cabinet approves One Network, Smarter Traffic: Delhi Moves to Real-Time Traffic Management
subtitle:

AI-enabled adaptive traffic signals, technology-based enforcement and real-time traffic information to make travel safer, smoother and more efficient 42 traffic corridors of Delhi to be covered in three phases

System to facilitate priority movement of ambulances and quicker response to congestion and road incidents
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 SEP 2026 3:18PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA), chaired by the  Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, has approved implementation of the ITMS Project by Delhi Police at an estimated cost of Rs.1,789.52 crore, inclusive of taxes. The project will cover 42 identified traffic corridors and will be implemented in three phases over 24 months, followed by five years of operation and maintenance.
As part of the wider efforts of the Central Government and the Government of NCT of Delhi to improve traffic management, transport infrastructure and urban mobility in the National Capital, a major technology-led initiative will now be taken up through the Intelligent Traffic Management System (ITMS). The project will enable Delhi’s existing road network to be managed more intelligently through real-time traffic data, adaptive traffic signals, automated enforcement and integrated command-and-control systems.
Delhi has around 71 lakh active registered vehicles. Vehicular growth has substantially outpaced expansion of road infrastructure, while traffic regulation continues to depend significantly on fixed signal timings and manual intervention. The ITMS seeks to make better use of the available road capacity by enabling traffic management to respond dynamically to actual conditions on the road.
Benefits:
Smarter traffic signals and smoother movement:
Adaptive Traffic Control Systems will dynamically adjust signal timings according to prevailing traffic conditions and coordinate signals along identified corridors, helping reduce avoidable stoppages and delays.
Priority for ambulances and emergency vehicles:
The system will facilitate green corridors and priority movement for emergency vehicles, enabling faster passage through congested stretches.
Faster response to congestion and accidents:
Real-time detection of congestion, slow-moving traffic and road incidents will enable quicker diversions and operational response by Delhi Police.
Timely information for commuters:
Variable Message Sign boards and digital platforms will provide information on congestion, diversions, parking availability and traffic conditions. Information may also be shared with navigation service providers, helping commuters make better travel choices.
More consistent and technology-based enforcement:
The system will strengthen automated detection of violations such as red-light and stop-line violations, speeding, wrong-way driving, non-use of helmets and seat belts, illegal parking and use of mobile phones while driving. AI-based analytics will also assist in identifying stolen, hot-listed and blacklisted vehicles, repeat violators and vehicles connected with hit-and-run incidents.
Integrated city-wide traffic management:
Traffic regulation, enforcement and information dissemination will be brought together on a common platform through Traffic Command and Control Centres, supported by secure Data Centre and Disaster Recovery infrastructure. The system will follow open standards and APIs to enable future integration and scalability.
The project will cover 1,092 Adaptive Traffic Control System and 1,029 enforcement locations. Implementation will be performance-driven, with each subsequent phase to be taken up after evaluation of the preceding phase against prescribed testing, commissioning, acceptance and performance parameters.
Delhi Police will implement the project through a Master System Integrator selected through competitive bidding. C-DAC will provide technical support as Project Management Consultant, including technical scrutiny, monitoring, validation and acceptance during implementation and operation and maintenance.
The ITMS will complement ongoing efforts to improve Delhi’s road and transport infrastructure by providing the technology and real-time intelligence required to use the existing road network more efficiently. The project is expected to contribute to smoother traffic movement, safer roads, quicker incident response, more effective enforcement and a more predictable travel experience for citizens.

The programme concluded with a second interactive question-and-answer session, during which participants engaged directly with the speakers and sought clarifications on various aspects of the Labour Codes, employer compliance, and social security schemes.

Minerals such as cobalt, nickel, manganese, copper and rare earth elements are important inputs for electric mobility, renewable energy systems, advanced electronics and strategic industries. Development of domestic offshore mineral resources can therefore contribute to India’s objectives of self-reliance, resource security and sustainable economic growth.
The auction is being conducted under the provisions of the Offshore Areas Mineral (Development and Regulation) Act, 2002 and the Offshore Areas Mineral (Auction) Rules, 2024, as amended from time to time. The auction comprises two offshore mineral blocks in the Andaman Sea region, which will be offered for grant of Composite Licence. It is expected to encourage systematic exploration, attract investment and promote the adoption of advanced technologies for offshore mineral exploration and development.
The initiative reflects the Government’s commitment to expanding India’s mineral resource base through systematic exploration and responsible development of offshore resources. It is also expected to facilitate greater private sector participation and technological innovation in an emerging area with significant potential for meeting future industrial and strategic requirements.
The launch of the auction marks another step towards harnessing India’s offshore mineral wealth and strengthening the country’s mineral security for emerging technologies, industrial development and long-term economic growth.

title: Cabinet approves Green Energy Corridor Phase-III scheme for Development of Intra-State Transmission System with Battery Energy Storage Systems
ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 SEP 2026 3:13PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Union Cabinet chaired by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi has approved the Green Energy Corridor Phase-III
(GEC-III) scheme. This historic initiative will strengthen India’s Intra-State Transmission System (InSTS) to enable evacuation of up to 135 Gigawatt (GW) of renewable energy across States/ Union Territories.
The scheme also provides for deployment of 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) at the Renewable Energy (RE) developer/generator end or any other location of importance for grid flexibility to address intermittency, congestion, peak-hour curtailment and meet non-solar hour demand. The scheme will facilitate grid integration and power evacuation with in the States/UTs of India.
The scheme is targeted to be set up by FY 2032-33 with total project outlay of Rs.1,86,405 crore, comprising Rs.1,36,378 crore for the development of Intra-State Transmission Systems (InSTS) under GEC-III, Rs.50,000 crore for 50 GWh of Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). The Scheme involves a total Central Financial Support of Rs.54,082 crore. The Central Financial Assistance (CFA) will help in offsetting the Intra-State transmission charges and thus keep the power costs down. Thus, the Government support will ultimately benefit the end users – the citizens of India.
All Greenfield projects under the InSTS component will be implemented through Tariff Based Competitive Bidding (TBCB) mode, while brownfield upgradation and network strengthening works will be executed under Cost Plus Basis (CPB). The State Transmission Utilities will be the overall implementing agency, and Transmission Service Providers (TSPs) will participate under TBCB on a Build-Own-Operate-Maintain (BOOM) model.
The scheme will help in achieving the target of 900 GW installed Non-Fossil capacity by 2035. The scheme will also contribute to long term energy security of the country and promote ecologically sustainable growth by reducing carbon footprint. It will generate large direct & indirect employment in the power sector, manufacturing, and construction industries. Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) manufacturing and deployment will additionally generate employment in the domestic energy storage industry. The scheme will also generate long-term skilled employment in operation, maintenance, and grid management across participating States.

Dr. Ajay Kumar said that the Commission must change what needs to change so that what must never change can be preserved. While technology and examination formats can evolve, the core constitutional principles of merit, fairness and equal opportunity remain enduring.
The Chairman highlighted the scale and diversity of the Commission’s work, noting that UPSC undertakes approximately 250 distinct recruitment processes every year, covering disciplines ranging from engineering, medical and scientific fields to economics and defence. He also highlighted that the UPSC examination calendar is prepared 18 months in advance, reflecting the extensive planning required for its recruitment processes.
Looking ahead, Dr. Ajay Kumar outlined several initiatives aimed at strengthening the recruitment ecosystem. These include the proposed establishment of a Centre of Excellence to facilitate collaboration and sharing of best practices with State Public Service Commissions. He also referred to the partnership with NALSAR, Hyderabad, for preparation of a compendium of 100 landmark judicial verdicts.
On examination reforms, the Chairman emphasised the importance of assessing candidates for qualities such as reasoning, spontaneous thinking and judgment under ambiguity, rather than their ability to reproduce predictable or coached model answers. He also highlighted the use of digital e-admit cards and face authentication as measures to strengthen examination integrity.
The first session of the centenary deliberations was held on the theme “Role of Civil Services in Viksit Bharat” under the leadership of Smt. Suman Sharma, Member, UPSC. The session brought together Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani, Chief of Defence Staff; Shri Harsh Vardhan Shringla, Member of Parliament (Rajya Sabha) and former Foreign Secretary; and Shri Sanjay Shrinet, Chairman, Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission.
Smt. Suman Sharma emphasised the need for outcome-driven administration and highlighted the role of civil servants as primary instruments for translating policy into ground-level outcomes. She called for a shift from procedural excuses towards proactive facilitation and for measuring administration through transformative outcomes on the ground rather than merely through financial expenditure.
Gen. N.S. Raja Subramani highlighted the need to overcome departmental silos, take intelligent risks and demonstrate decisiveness in an environment marked by rapid disruption and increasing civil-military convergence. He underlined the need for an agile and problem-solving civil service.
Shri Harsh Vardhan Shringla emphasised the importance of widening recruitment into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities and aspirational districts, as well as bringing younger candidates into public service. He also referred to the principles of Antyodaya and Nishkama Karma, stressing the responsibility of public servants to serve the last person in the queue.
Shri Sanjay Shrinet emphasised that reforms should empower the grassroots machinery responsible for executing public programmes, noting that the overwhelming majority of the administrative machinery is below Group A level. He called for a shift from authority to accountability and highlighted the importance of administrators functioning as genuine public servants or Sevaks.
Delivering the keynote address at the panel discussion on “Public Service Commissions as a Constitutional Body,” Dr. Ashok Lahiri reflected on the UPSC’s centenary journey and its enduring role in nation-building. He traced the historical evolution of public recruitment from early patronage systems to an impartial constitutional framework rooted in merit, competitive examinations, fairness, and transparency—spanning its milestones from the Public Service Commission in 1926 to the Federal Public Service Commission in 1937, and finally its constitutional status in 1950. Dr. Lahiri underscored the Commission's vital constitutional mandate in upholding equality, justice, and public trust, while highlighting its essential responsibilities beyond recruitment to encompass promotions, service rules, and disciplinary matters
The second session, titled “Innovations in Public Service”, was chaired by Lt Gen Raj Shukla (Retd.), Member, UPSC. Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, delivered the keynote address.
Delivering the keynote address in the second session, Shri Shaktikanta Das, Principal Secretary-2 to the Prime Minister, commended the UPSC as the “gateway to public service,” lauding its steadfast commitment to integrity, fairness, and perseverance in the selection process. He highlighted key administrative initiatives and innovations introduced by the Government, while outlining a strategic roadmap to advance the vision of Viksit Bharat.
The discussions highlighted the potential of Artificial Intelligence, data analytics and digital architectures to reduce bureaucratic friction and optimise service delivery. The session also emphasised the need for government systems to respond in real time to a confident, aspirational and digitally literate population.
The deliberations further underscored the importance of breaking bureaucratic compartmentalisation, encouraging cross-departmental learning and building a future-ready civil service equipped to respond to emerging challenges.
The centenary discussions also reflected on the Commission’s continuing adoption of technology. UPSC’s technology journey has evolved over several decades, beginning with the introduction of computers in 1978, followed by successive technological interventions in its examination and recruitment processes.
More recent reforms include the introduction of the Universal Registration Number in 2025, randomised interview boards, a dedicated Candidate Helpdesk with a 30-channel IP call centre and a two-level escalation mechanism, and the expansion of examination centres.
In 2026, new examination centres were introduced at Bhubaneswar, Kanpur and Meerut for Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination and at Alwar, Hisar and Kinnaur for NDA & NA (II). The Commission also introduced measures relating to provisional answer keys and the QPRep portal.
The Commission has been strengthening its digital infrastructure and cybersecurity capabilities, while officers are also being trained in emerging technologies, including Artificial Intelligence. A High-Level Network Committee has been constituted for IT infrastructure and cybersecurity-related requirements.
A significant technological initiative has been the introduction of AI-based facial authentication. Following a pilot at select centres in Gurugram during the NDA & NA (II) and CDS (II) examinations in September 2025, the system was implemented at scale for the Civil Services (Preliminary) Examination on 24 May 2026, covering approximately 5.50 lakh candidates. The system uses invigilators’ mobile phones for facial authentication, with the process taking approximately six to eight seconds per candidate.
The centenary also marks a century-long institutional journey that began on 1 October 1926, when the first Public Service Commission in India was constituted as an advisory body. Over the decades, the institution evolved into an independent constitutional body.
The constitutional framework governing Public Service Commissions is contained in Part XIV of the Constitution, under Articles 315 to 323. These provisions establish Public Service Commissions for the Union and the States and provide safeguards relating to the appointment, tenure and removal of their members.
The constitutional framework also provides for the functions of the Commission, including conducting examinations for recruitment to Union services and advising on methods of recruitment, promotions and disciplinary matters. The expenses of the Commission are charged on the Consolidated Fund, while the Commission submits an annual report to the President, including cases where its advice has not been accepted.
In carrying out its mandate, UPSC also advises the Government on Recruitment Rules, promotions through Departmental Promotion Committees, induction into the All-India Services and disciplinary cases. During 2023-24, the Commission processed records relating to 24,581 officers for promotion and 532 officers were inducted into the All-India Services.

title: NEW CORPORATE AVERAGE FUEL ECONOMY (CAFE) NORMS NOTIFIED
subtitle:
SEEKS OVER 16% IMPROVEMENT IN FUEL EFFICIENCY OVER 5 YEARS

SUPPORTS DEVELOPMENT OF ALTERNATIVE FUELS, EVs AND HYBRID CARS

PROMOTES INNOVATIONS IN NEW TECHNOLOGIES FOR HIGHER ENERGY EFFICIENCY IN CARS
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 SEP 2026 9:57AM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Power, Government of India has notified the new Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) Norms for passenger vehicles, which will come into effect from 1 April 2027 and remain applicable up to 31 March 2032. The new norms will apply to new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India.
The new CAFE framework will drive progressive improvements in fuel economy through year-on-year tightening of targets across all five years. The fuel-consumption benchmark is tightened from 3.996 litres/100 km in 2027–28 to 3.3273 litres/100 km in 2031–32, representing an improvement of around 16.7 per cent over the period.
The revised target line has also been flattened to provide a more balanced, weight sensitive approach, with relatively softer targets for lighter vehicles and greater fuel efficiency requirements for heavier vehicles. The reference weight has been increased from 1,082 kg under existing norms to 1,229 kg under new CAFE norms, an increase of around 13.6 per cent, reflecting the evolving characteristics of the passenger vehicle fleet.
The new norms provide flexibility to manufacturers to adopt cleaner technologies, alternative fuels and other innovative solutions. The new CAFE framework promotes technological innovation in new technologies such as Solar reflective paints, advance glazing, high efficiency air-conditioning for improved fuel efficiency and India’s energy security and sustainability objectives.
The passenger vehicle segment accounts for a substantial share of India's transport energy demand and remains an important contributor to fossil-fuel consumption. The new CAFÉ framework is consistent with and supports, rapid technological advancements, increasing availability of alternative and renewable fuels, growing electrification and evolving global automotive technologies.
Explanatory Note
Corporate Average Fuel Economy (CAFE) Norms from 2027-28 to 2031-32: A Future-Ready and Flexible Framework for India's Automotive Sector
The new CAFE Norms notified today, will apply to passenger vehicles for the period from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2032. They will replace the existing CAFE norms with effect from 1 April 2027 and will apply to new passenger vehicles manufactured or imported for sale in India. The new framework provides greater regulatory clarity and a stable policy framework for the automobile industry, while facilitating technological innovation and supporting the continued evolution of India’s passenger vehicle sector towards greater energy efficiency and lower fuel consumption.
CAFE framework marks an important milestone in India’s transition towards cleaner, more energy-efficient and sustainable mobility. The new CAFE Norms have been finalised following extensive consultations with automobile manufacturers, industry associations, academia and other stakeholders, with the objective of providing a future-ready, technology-neutral and flexible regulatory framework for the passenger vehicle sector.
The CAFE framework builds on the gains achieved under the existing regime while providing greater technology choice, flexibility and regulatory certainty to the automotive industry.
The framework seeks to drive continuous improvements in fuel efficiency while enabling greater adoption of cleaner technologies, alternative fuels and innovative solutions, thereby supporting India’s energy security and sustainability objectives. The framework is aligned with the broader vision articulated by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi for clean, energy-efficient and sustainable mobility as an important pillar of India’s development and energy security.
Key Features of the new CAFE Norms
1. The overall fleet-average target has been progressively strengthened compared with the existing targets, while simultaneously providing manufacturers with a range of incentives and compliance pathways to encourage the adoption of clean fuels, cleaner technologies and more efficient vehicles. The framework therefore combines higher ambition with greater flexibility for industry to determine the most appropriate technology pathways.
2. The framework recognises the contribution of renewable and low-carbon fuels, including ethanol-blended petrol, biofuels and CBG, through the introduction of the Carbon Neutrality Factor (CNF). This provides manufacturers with an additional pathway for improving their fleet-level CAFE performance, alongside vehicle efficiency improvements and electrification. The provision supports India's broader transition towards cleaner fuels while encouraging innovation across multiple technology pathways.
3. The list of recognised fuel-conservation technologies has been significantly expanded from four to twelve technologies. This provides manufacturers with greater flexibility to adopt and receive recognition for approved fuel-saving technologies. A concession of 1 g CO₂/km for each eligible technology, subject to a maximum of 9.0 g CO₂/km, is available under the framework.
4. Battery Electric Vehicles (BEVs), Range-Extended Electric Vehicles (REEVs), Plug-in Hybrid Electric Vehicles (PHEVs), Strong Hybrid Electric Vehicles(SHEV) and Flex-Fuel Vehicles will receive volume derogation factors, also known as ‘super credits’, in fleet-average calculations. This provides an additional incentive for manufacturers to accelerate the deployment and market penetration of cleaner and advanced vehicle technologies.
5. To facilitate ease of compliance and provide manufacturers with greater operational flexibility, manufacturers may opt to meet their obligations over specified two-year/three-year compliance blocks, as provided under the framework. This allows manufacturers greater flexibility in managing their technology transition and product portfolios over the compliance period.
6. The framework provides greater flexibility to manufacturers in meeting their CAFE obligations. Manufacturers that perform better than their prescribed targets will generate credits, which may be carried forward within the specified compliance blocks. Manufacturers with a compliance gap may utilise eligible carry-forward provisions, enter into exchange/trade of credits with other manufacturers, or purchase credits through the buyout mechanism administered by the Bureau of Energy Efficiency. These provisions are intended to ease the compliance burden, provide flexibility during the transition and enable manufacturers to manage variations in their product portfolio and technology adoption pathways.
7. Reporting will be undertaken under both the Modified Indian Driving Cycle (MIDC) and the Worldwide Harmonized Light Vehicles Test Procedure (WLTP). This dual approach will facilitate India's gradual transition towards globally harmonised vehicle testing practices.
8. Manufacturers with annual sales of below 1,000 units will remain exempt from fleet-average obligations, thereby avoiding the regulatory burden for low-volume manufacturers.

title: NHAI to Conduct Special Quality Checks on Projects with Abnormally Low Quoted Bids
subtitle: Project inspections to strengthen quality, ensure compliance with technical standards and facilitate timely corrective action
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                30 SEP 2026 4:55PM by PIB Delhi
content:
To strengthen quality control and adherence to the highest quality standards during construction of National Highway projects, National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) is undertaking special quality inspections of 17 under construction National Highway projects, whose bid value was lower than the estimated project cost by over 15 percent.  The inspections are in addition to NHAI’s regular quality checks and are aimed at identifying any quality-related issues at an early stage so that corrective action can be taken on time. The first round of inspections is scheduled to be completed by December 2026. NHAI will re-inspect the identified projects after 6 months with a different team of experts to ensure quality and adherence to construction standards.
17 projects selected based on specific criteria
The 17 projects have been selected using three criteria: construction cost of more than ₹500 crore, tender discount of over 15% and physical progress between 35% and 80%. These criteria help focus quality checks on projects that are at an important stage of construction and adopt an objective, data-driven approach.
The projects include greenfield and access-controlled corridors, bypasses, as well as four and six laning works in the states of Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Haryana, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh.
Experienced engineers to conduct inspections
In order to reinforce quality mechanism and ensure compliance, NHAI has created a pool of experts. The inspections will be carried out by specialised teams led by 39 experienced and retired engineers from various government organisations, including the Ministry of Road Transport & Highways, Ministry of Railways, Ministry of Defence and State Public Works Departments. Technical experts will also support the teams during the inspections.
Quality of construction, materials and safety to be checked
The teams will check construction work against approved drawings, technical specifications, contract conditions and project-specific quality plans. They will examine the quality of construction materials, workmanship, construction methods as well as records of sampling and testing.
The inspections will also cover road safety measures, traffic management and environmental safeguards, wherever applicable. Any work that does not meet the required standards will be identified and followed up for corrective action as per the applicable contract provisions.
The specialised inspections will also help NHAI to identify common quality issues, construction practices and areas where greater accountability is required from contractors, consultants and other project stakeholders.
The initiative is part of NHAI’s continued efforts to strengthen quality monitoring of ongoing National Highway projects and ensure timely corrective action, with the objective of developing a world class National Highway network across the country.
